pencereler.0-5: Every bridge is fighting a quiet war against physics. The biggest enemy is not
pencereler.5-12: weight. It is the wind. Wind can make a deck twist, and at the wrong speed that motion feeds
pencereler.12-20: on itself. Engineers call this flutter, and it tore apart the Tacoma Narrows Bridge. Metal also gets tired. Every single flex leaves
pencereler.20-30: a tiny crack. Over the years those cracks spread until the metal simply gives way. Add rust, overloading, or one weak bolt, and the whole thing can fail.

segmentler.metin: Every bridge is fighting a quiet war against physics.
It took only wind, fatigue and corrosion.
The answer is metal fatigue and aeroelastic flutter — and it is why bridges are wind-tunnel tested and inspected for cracks.
